aarti.tek: Om, victory to Śiva, who is the sacred syllable Om; victory, O Lord, to Śiva who is Om! You are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Sadāśiva, and you bear your consort as half of your body.
aarti.pad1: You shine with one face (as Viṣṇu), four faces (as Brahmā) and five faces (as Śiva), adorned with the swan seat, the Garuḍa seat and the bull for a mount.
aarti.pad2: With two arms, four arms and ten arms you look most beautiful; beholding your form of the three guṇas, the people of the three worlds are enchanted.
aarti.pad3: You wear the rosary of beads, the garland of forest flowers and the garland of skulls; you are the foe of Tripura and the foe of Kaṁsa, and hold a rosary in your hand.
aarti.pad4: White robes, yellow silk and a tiger skin are on your limbs; Sanaka and the sages, Garuḍa and the rest, and the bhūtas are your companions.
aarti.pad5: In your hands are the water pot, the discus and the trident; you are the maker of the world, its sustainer and its destroyer.
aarti.pad6: The undiscerning see Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Sadāśiva as separate; in the syllable Om the three shine as one, and this is the crowning mark of the three Vedas.
aarti.pad7: O Śiva, the syllable Om; O Hara, the syllable Om! You are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Sadāśiva, bearing your consort as half of your body.
